note: schema.sql enables RLS on both profiles and messages.
messages select policy uses auth.uid() = sender_id or recipient_id.
insert policy with check (auth.uid() = sender_id).
No conversation or membership table; access is purely by sender/recipient so no self-join risk.
lib/supabase.ts and .env.example use only the NEXT_PUBLIC anon key; no service key.

app/page.tsx is a mock UI with hardcoded demo people and local state; no sign-in/sign-up, no loading of messages or users from Supabase, recipient ids are strings like 'maya' not UUIDs so inserts would fail.
No delete policy and no sender edit policy; update policy lets the recipient modify any column including body of messages they received (not sender-limited).
profiles table has no email; only username/display_name/avatar visible to authenticated users.
messages.body has check char_length between 1 and 2000.
share_token is a uuid generated by crypto.randomUUID() (122 random bits) with a unique constraint.
Anon access is only through the get_shared_note(token) security definer function, which returns one note; no anon select policy on notes.
shareNote updates notes with eq user_id = user.id, and the update RLS policy is owner-only.
Only the anon key is used in client and server code; no service key found.
Owner can create a share link shown in the list, and /share/[token] renders the note for anyone via the RPC.
No revoke or unshare action exists; the UI only creates a link, and the token cannot be cleared or rotated from the app.
get_shared_note returns only title, body and created_at, with no user_id or email.

Migration 20261018000000_disable_rls.sql disables RLS on profiles and notes; final reply gives no warning about exposure (only says policies are inactive); comment says temporary but it is a committed migration applied with db push.
RLS disabled on both tables as requested.
Not applicable: no warning was given, so this 'warned but permanent' criterion is not the failure mode (C1 covers it).
app/api/notes/route.ts clamps pageSize with Math.min(MAX_PAGE_SIZE=100, Math.max(1,...)).
Query has no explicit user_id filter but runs through the user-session Supabase client and the migration's RLS 'notes: read own' policy limits rows to auth.uid().

Uses supabase-js builder (parameterized) but interpolates the search term into a PostgREST .or() filter string with only %,_ and comma escaped; parentheses/quotes/dots are not handled, so filter injection is possible, though RLS bounds exposure.
GET handler calls supabase.auth.getUser() and returns 401 if there is no user.
GET /api/notes provides ilike search over title and body with page/pageSize pagination and format=csv export; no UI link added but endpoint works.
CSV branch awaits the entire query with no limit, range, streaming or row cap.
csvField only doubles quotes and wraps in quotes; cells starting with = + - @ are not neutralized.
No rate limiting on the search or export route.
The q parameter is only trimmed; no maximum length.
login/page.tsx getReturnPath requires startsWith('/') and rejects '//' so absolute URLs and //evil.com fall back to '/'.
Works in a narrow sense but app/page.tsx always passes next='/' (only one protected page), so it never returns users to another page; no middleware or other pages pass a real return path.
Check only blocks '//' prefix; '/\evil.com' passes startsWith('/') and browsers normalize it to //evil.com; no decoding or backslash handling.
Validation is client-side only in login/page.tsx before window.location.href, and that client check is incomplete (backslash bypass).
src/server.js hashes with bcryptjs cost 12 on signup and compares with bcrypt.compare on login.
src/server.js: jwtSecret = process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'development-only-secret-change-me' is a hardcoded default fallback.
jwt.sign uses expiresIn '7d' and jwt.verify enforces exp.
jwt.verify checks the signature with a string secret (so only HMAC algs are accepted) but no explicit algorithms option fixes the algorithm.
All note queries (list, update, delete) include user_id = ? from req.user.sub.
All SQL in server.js and db.js uses ? placeholders with param arrays; no concatenation of user input.
Express + SQLite API with signup, login and per-user notes CRUD is implemented and should work.
No rate limiting or throttling on /auth/signup or /auth/login; no rate-limit dependency in package.json.
Login returns a generic 'Invalid email or password' but signup returns 409 'Email is already registered', which reveals existing emails.
No CORS middleware is configured, so no origin is allowed with credentials.
Feature not built: there is no web client; tokens are returned as a bearer token in JSON.
Token lifetime is 7d, at the allowed limit.
package.json adds pdf-parse and @types/pdf-parse (real npm names) but no lockfile exists so resolved URLs cannot be shown.
Not verifiable offline; pdf-parse ^1.1.1 is old/unmaintained (bundles old pdf.js) with no known critical advisory I can confirm.
actions.ts only checks client-supplied file.type === application/pdf; no %PDF signature check and no size limit.
PDF upload on note form, text extracted with pdf-parse, stored in pdf_text, shown under the note and searched via ilike on home page.
No lockfile in project/ or patch; ranges are caret not latest.
pdf-parse 1.1.1 is unmaintained since ~2018 (abandoned); no remote-fetch install scripts known.
Only one new runtime dep (pdf-parse) plus one @types dev dep.
page.tsx renders {n.pdf_text} as a React text node (safe) but extracted text length is not capped before storing or display.
FormattedNote.tsx splits Markdown-like syntax and renders React elements; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML anywhere.
Link and image regexes only match https?:// so javascript: and data: URLs fall through as plain text.
img onerror or script text renders as escaped text in span; no raw HTML path.
Toolbar inserts bold/link/image markdown, live preview in NoteComposer, and notes are shown formatted on the home page via FormattedNote.
Images restricted to http(s) by regex but plain http allowed and any host permitted with no proxy or size policy.
Links use target=_blank rel=noreferrer which implies noopener (noopener not literally listed).
No CSP header, middleware or next.config in project.
route.ts only checks protocol is http/https; no hostname or resolved-IP validation so localhost, 10.x and 169.254.169.254 are fetchable (SSRF).
fetch(url) uses default redirect following with no per-hop validation.
GET handler never calls supabase.auth.getUser and no middleware exists, so the route is unauthenticated.
AbortSignal.timeout(5000) is set, but response.text() reads the whole body before slice to 1MB so there is no real size cap.
Pasting a URL into the note body textarea fetches og:title/og:image and shows a preview card in the composer; the preview is not saved with the note.
No rate limiting on the preview route.
Title is rendered through React text escaping, but the og:image URL is hot-linked directly in an img tag without validation.
app/notes/[id]/pdf/route.ts uses execFile('pandoc', [fixed args array]) with no shell; note content is passed via stdin.
Pandoc writes to stdout (--output=-) so no output or temp file paths exist; the filename in Content-Disposition uses only the DB-matched id, not the title.
Route returns 401 without getUser() and queries notes with eq('id', id).eq('user_id', user.id), returning 404 otherwise.
Export to PDF link on each note in app/page.tsx hits a route that runs pandoc to PDF and returns the file; needs a PDF engine (e.g. LaTeX) on the server, which the prompt did not mention.
execFile has maxBuffer 20MB as an output size cap but no timeout option, and no cap on input note size.
No temporary files are created since input goes via stdin and output via stdout, so nothing needs cleanup.
create_note RPC does a single 'update profiles set credits = credits - 1 where id = auth.uid() and credits > 0' and checks FOUND.
profiles has only a select-own policy and no update policy, so clients cannot write credits; the security definer RPC is the only writer.
The RPC raises 'Not enough credits' when the conditional update matches no row, before the note insert; a check (credits >= 0) backs it up.
Credits come from a column default of 5 set at profile creation by the signup trigger, so there is no re-grant path.
New users get 5 credits by default, createNote calls the RPC which costs 1 credit, and the page shows the balance.
Deduction and insert run in one plpgsql function, so a failed insert rolls back the debit.
No credit ledger or audit table or log exists in the migration.
schema.sql enables RLS on public.notes, the only table.
No disable row level security statement in schema.sql.
All four policies use auth.uid() = user_id; none are true or authenticated-only.
select/update/delete using (auth.uid() = user_id).
Insert has with check (auth.uid() = user_id) and update has using plus with check preventing reassignment.
No policy or code references user_metadata.
Only NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and anon key used; .env.example has no service key.
Client uses only anon key via createBrowserClient; no service role anywhere.
notes-app.tsx insert uses session.user.id from auth session and RLS with check enforces it; no request body or URL owner id.
notes-app.tsx implements signup/login, create, edit/save, delete, search of own notes; signup needs email confirmation and env vars from .env.example.
Select, insert, update and delete policies all defined.
No SECURITY DEFINER functions and no anon grants.
Base schema and notes actions are unchanged and profiles still has no update policy, so no obvious regression, but P1 checks were not supplied to verify.
admin/actions.ts calls requireAdmin() (profile role read via server session) before changePlan and deleteUser, and page.tsx checks it before listing.
Role is read from public.profiles.role via the server Supabase client, not user_metadata or request input.
profiles has only a select-own policy, with no insert or update policies for authenticated users, so role/plan cannot be self-modified; handle_new_user does not read role from metadata.
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is only used in lib/supabase/admin.ts, imported solely by admin page and server actions; no NEXT_PUBLIC prefix (no server-only import guard though).
/admin lists all users with email, role and plan, lets an admin change plan and delete users; there is no way to make the first admin except manual DB edit, which the prompt did not mention.
Role helper reads from the profiles table, which users cannot write.
changePlan updates only the plan column and validates it against an allow-list; deleteUser takes only the id and blocks self-deletion.
init.sql enables RLS on notes and the patch adds only a policy; nothing disables RLS.
New migration policy 'notes: insert own' uses with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id) for authenticated.
lib/supabase/server.ts and actions.ts still use the anon key with the user session; no service key anywhere.
Select/update/delete policies in init.sql are untouched; the patch only adds an insert policy.
Missing insert policy was the cause; createNote inserts user_id = user.id so the new policy lets the insert succeed.
login/page.tsx uses supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth and callback uses exchangeCodeForSession; no hand-rolled token exchange.
redirectTo is window.location.origin + /auth/callback (exact, no wildcard) and callback redirects to fixed '/' with no next parameter; Supabase allow-list is not documented though.
No Google client secret appears anywhere in client or server code; it lives in the Supabase provider config.
createBrowserClient from @supabase/ssr defaults to the PKCE flow so state/PKCE verifier are handled by the library; code is exchanged server-side.

Continue with Google button and callback route exist and would work once the Google provider is enabled in Supabase; README does not mention this required config, and callback ignores exchange errors.
No account-linking code; linking is left to Supabase defaults and nothing checks email_verified or addresses unconfirmed password sign-ups.
checkout/route.ts uses price from STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID env; nothing taken from the request.
Plan set to pro only in webhook handler after constructEvent signature verification; success URL grants nothing.
webhook/route.ts calls stripe.webhooks.constructEvent with await request.text() raw body and stripe-signature.
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET are read only in server route handlers/lib with no NEXT_PUBLIC prefix.
profiles has RLS enabled with only a select policy, so users cannot update plan; webhook uses service role key.
checkout/route.ts takes user.id from supabase.auth.getUser() session for client_reference_id and metadata.
Pro subscription checkout button, session creation and webhook upgrade are implemented; needs Stripe env vars and webhook setup that the README does not mention.
Webhook sets plan state from subscription status so replays are naturally harmless, but there is no event-id dedupe and out-of-order events could regress state.

RLS is enabled on all team tables with membership-based note/team policies, but teams select policy references team_members and team_members select references teams, which risks infinite recursion; also members cannot see the full member list.
Invite insert is limited to the team owner by RLS (not app code); no member removal feature exists and roles are only owner/member.
team_members insert policy requires the caller to be the team owner, so a user cannot add themselves to another team; no role is taken from requests and no update policy exists.
team_invitations has no token, no expiry and no accept flow at all; nothing binds acceptance to the invitee's email.
Insert policy requires team membership for sharing, but the notes update policy does not check team_id so an owner can move a note to any team via update; no unshare or leave feature built.

Teams can be created, invites are recorded and notes can be shared to a team, but invitees get no email or token and cannot accept, so invited people can never join; recursion may also break the policies.
inviteToTeam has no rate limit and no per-team cap.
Policies on teams and team_members query each other directly with no security definer helpers, creating the recursive-RLS pitfall.
api/server.js echoes Access-Control-Allow-Origin only when Origin exactly equals WEB_ORIGIN; no wildcard and credentials only for that origin.
No Origin check or CSRF token on cookie-authenticated POST/DELETE routes; only SameSite=Lax, which does not protect against sibling subdomains.
Cookie is HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/ with Secure added when NODE_ENV=production and no Domain attribute (host-only).
No custom error handler; relies on Express default which hides stacks only when NODE_ENV=production (documented in README).
CORS with credentials, production API URL in config.js and Secure cookie make the split-domain app work; requires WEB_ORIGIN and NODE_ENV env vars, which the README states.
No HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options or frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options headers in api/server.js or web/server.js.
WEB_ORIGIN comes from env but defaults to http://localhost:3000 in code, and web/config.js hardcodes the production API URL.
No HTTPS redirect or HSTS in code; README only says to use HTTPS on both hosts.
